subject: Oceanography
title: The Biological Pump
description: A fast breakdown of The Biological Pump for builders.

hook.text: Tiny plankton in the surface ocean pull CO₂ from the air—then sink when they die, locking carbon in the deep.

buildup.text: Phytoplankton photosynthesize like plants—converting dissolved CO₂ into organic carbon.

discovery.text: When they die or are eaten, carbon rains downward as 'marine snow'—sinking to the deep ocean floor.

twist.text: Only about 1% of surface carbon reaches the deep—but over millennia, this pump has stored vast carbon reserves.

climax.text: If the biological pump weakened, CO₂ would build up faster in the atmosphere—accelerating warming.

punchline.text: Plankton are Earth's smallest carbon couriers—delivering CO₂ to the abyss.

quiz.question: What is the biological pump?
options: Plankton absorbing CO₂ and sinking carbon to the deep ocean
A machine that extracts carbon from seawater
